title: Panacea Biotec Gets Rs 9.82 Crore Income Tax Penalty Demand Over Alleged Income Misreporting

contentHtml:
New Delhi: Panacea Biotec Limited has received four demand orders from the Office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Delhi, imposing an aggregate penalty demand of approximately Rs 9.82 crore over alleged misreporting or under-reporting of income for multiple assessment years.

According to the company’s disclosure dated September 26, 2026, the demand orders were issued under Section 156 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, and were dated September 25, 2026. Panacea Biotec received the four orders on September 26, 2026. The company made the disclosure pursuant to Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) Regulations, 2015.

The orders relate to assessment years 2014-15 to 2016-17 and 2018-19. As detailed in the company’s Annexure A, the Income Tax Department has raised an aggregate demand of approximately ₹9.82 crore towards penalties arising from alleged misreporting or under-reporting of income.

The department has alleged misreporting or under-reporting of income in assessment orders passed earlier and has imposed the penalty under Section 270A of the Income Tax Act. The company, however, has stated that, based on its assessment, the demand is not maintainable.

Panacea Biotec has further disclosed that it is taking all necessary steps in relation to the demand, including filing an appeal before the appellate authority. The company has stated that it does not envisage any significant impact of the demand on its financial, operational or other activities. The company’s filing also records the details of any aberrations or non-compliances identified by the authority as “Not Applicable”.
